open_points.subject: A28
open_points.question: What exactly counts as a viewer-entry request for the one-reading rule: every HTTP attempt at the entry endpoint, only requests that reach the viewer-entry use case, or only attempts that pass parsing and preliminary validation?
options: Read once for every HTTP request targeting viewer entry, including malformed and transport-refused attempts.
Read once only when the request reaches the viewer-entry rate-limit component.
Read once only after the entry request passes parsing and preliminary validation.
open_points.default_guess: Read once whenever the viewer-entry rate-limit component is invoked; requests refused before that component take no elapsed reading.

witness.initial: The portal is running with a clock-source spy and viewer entry enabled.
events: A viewer sends a malformed request to the viewer-entry endpoint that is refused before credential verification.
The viewer then sends a well-formed viewer-entry request.
outcomes: The malformed attempt counts as a viewer-entry request, so the clock source records two monotonic readings.
Only invocation of the viewer-entry rate-limit component counts, so the clock source records one monotonic reading.
witness.observer: A verification check observing clock-source calls, and potentially the viewer if rejected attempts affect the later rate-limit window.

open_points.subject: A28
open_points.text: “Its one user is the viewer-entry rate limit of A25”
open_points.question: What must the CLK-002 Required test do to demonstrate that the viewer-entry rate limit is the only caller of the clock source’s monotonic reading?
options: Statically or architecturally prove that no other module calls the monotonic-reading port.
Exercise only the viewer-entry rate limit and assume that no other consumer exists.
Test every operation and assert that only viewer entry requests cause monotonic reads.
open_points.default_guess: Add an architectural check that the A25 viewer-entry rate limit is the sole caller of the monotonic-reading port, plus the behavioral per-request test.

witness.initial: The viewer-entry rate limit correctly uses one clock-source monotonic reading per request and passes the stated CLK-002 behavioral test.
events: Another module is implemented to call the same clock-source monotonic method for transient performance measurement without persisting or mixing the value with wall time.
The required CLK-002 test is run only against the A25 viewer-entry window.
outcomes: The implementation is rejected because A25 is required to be the monotonic reading’s sole user.
The implementation passes because the Required tests item never requires checking for other callers of the clock-source method.
witness.observer: The architecture verifier or a later maintainer adding another monotonic-clock consumer.

open_points.subject: A28
open_points.question: What must the CLK-002 Required test show to establish that monotonic readings and viewer-entry window state never cross a process boundary?
options: Assert that the reading and rate-limit window state remain entirely process-local.
Only assert that monotonic readings are not durably persisted.
Permit non-persistent inter-process transfer while forbidding durable storage.
open_points.default_guess: Require the monotonic reading and all window state derived from it to remain within the process that obtained the reading.

witness.initial: The viewer-entry rate limiter obtains one monotonic reading per request and never writes it to durable storage.
events: One process sends the reading or derived window state over IPC to another process.
The receiving process uses it when deciding a later viewer-entry request.
outcomes: The implementation is refused because elapsed readings must be used within one process.
The implementation passes the stated Required test because the reading was not persisted or mixed with wall-clock values.
witness.observer: A deployment using multiple worker processes and the verification suite.
